title: Nine Beasts or Ten? Only One Chinese Roof Has All 10 | China Travel Expert
description:
Look up at an old Chinese hall and you can read its rank from the roof — a line of little guardian figures marching down each ridge. The more there are, the more important the building.

The maximum anywhere in China is nine. Only one roof breaks that rule: the Hall of Supreme Harmony in the Forbidden City, which carries a tenth. That last figure is called the Hangshi (行什), and it sits on no other roof in the country — a quiet marker that this was the emperor's throne hall.

🧭 Expert Tip: at the Forbidden City, stand at the corner of the Hall of Supreme Harmony and count the crouching beasts down the ridge — ten is the giveaway you're looking at the top of the whole hierarchy.

看屋脊上的小兽就能读出等级——九是上限，只有紫禁城太和殿破例排到十，第十只叫"行什"，全中国别无二家。
